s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent embolic stroke in a child with a history of LVAD implantation and cardiac allograft
salient_findings: Compression of left bronchus and deviation of the tracheobronchial tree
key_facts: Patient is a 2-year-old girl
Patient has a history of paracorporeal continuous-flow LVAD implantation
Patient has undergone ambulatory rehabilitation
Patient requires frequent pump exchange
Patient's weight is 12 kg
Patient's height is 82 cm
Initial physical examination details are not provided
Computed Tomography shows maximal transverse diameter of left hemithorax of 9.4 cm
Post-operative CT scans show compression of left bronchus and deviation of the tracheobronchial tree
Echocardiography includes serial measurements of LVEF, left ventricular mass index, TAPSE, and TRPG

shortlist.label: Thromboembolism
shortlist.why_kept: History of embolic stroke and LVAD implantation

shortlist.label: LVAD thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of paracorporeal continuous-flow LVAD implantation and requires frequent pump exchange

shortlist.label: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has undergone cardiac allograft and has a history of embolic stroke

shortlist.label: Hypercoagulability disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent embolic stroke in a child suggests a possible underlying coagulation disorder

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent embolic events and potential association with cardiac allograft

raw.rationale: The patient's history of paracorporeal continuous-flow LVAD implantation and requirement for frequent pump exchange, along with episodes of embolic stroke, suggests a high likelihood of LVAD thrombosis as the cause of the embolic events.

rejected.label: Thromboembolism
rejected.why: Too general, as it does not specify the source of the thromboembolism

rejected.label: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy
rejected.why: The patient has an LVAD, not a cardiac transplant, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Hypercoagulability disorder
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of a hypercoagulable state, and the patient's symptoms are more directly related to the LVAD

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of antiphospholipid antibodies or other characteristic features of this syndrome
